source.title: Execute Workflow node panel shows stale sub-workflow restriction state after changing the selected sub-workflow

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

When opening an Execute Workflow node panel and selecting or switching the target sub-workflow, the restriction callout inside the node panel does not force a fresh policy check if the sub-workflow was already checked earlier in the session or if the workflow ID field started empty. If a sub-workflow's restricted node policies were updated since the workflow editor loaded, the node panel continues displaying the cached restriction state instead of fetching the current check.

### To Reproduce

1. Open a workflow containing an Execute Workflow node that points to Sub-Workflow A (or starts with an empty workflow ID), and also have Sub-Workflow B checked on the canvas.
2. Update Sub-Workflow B so it now contains (or no longer contains) a policy-restricted node.
3. Open the Execute Workflow node panel and change the selected sub-workflow to Sub-Workflow B.
4. Observe that no new sub-workflow policy check request is sent for Sub-Workflow B, and the callout in the node panel reflects the old cached state.

### Expected behavior

Selecting or changing the target sub-workflow inside the open Execute Workflow node panel should always fetch a fresh sub-workflow policy check for the newly selected sub-workflow.
